clue.text: Polish picture's old Italian border

parts.note: to polish is to rub, as with a cloth
an icon is a picture, especially a sacred image; the 's is 'has' joining the pieces

explanation.surface: A Polish painting depicts an ancient Italian frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb 'to polish'. The Rubicon was the river marking the border Caesar crossed into Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rubicon was the stream that formed the boundary between Roman Italy and Cisalpine Gaul.

clue.text: Journey possible on only one underground line

definitions.text: Journey possible on only one underground line

parts.words: Journey possible on only one underground line
parts.note: a journey ending where it began is natural on the London Underground's Circle line, which loops back on itself

explanation.surface: A trip that can be made using a single Tube line.
explanation.walkthrough: London's Circle line runs in a loop, so you can ride it out and back to your starting station without changing.
explanation.definitionFit: An outward and return journey brings the traveller back to the start, as a loop line does.

clue.text: Second record in reserve, still to be dealt with

definitions.text: reserve, still to be dealt with

parts.note: to second a motion is to back or support it
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A second recording kept in reserve, still awaiting attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a number or a unit of time, but it is the verb meaning to support.
explanation.definitionFit: Work accumulated and waiting to be handled forms a stock held over for later.

clue.text: Whistler visiting Tom?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
someone visiting is a caller

explanation.surface: Is the painter Whistler paying a visit to someone called Tom?
explanation.walkthrough: Whistler looks like the painter and Tom like a man's name; Tom is a tomcat, and the one visiting him is a caller. A whistler here jeers by whistling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who whistles derisively at a performer or passer-by is a jeerer of that kind.

clue.text: A flat, for example, for letter

definitions.meaning: A flat is a musical pitch written on the stave

explanation.definitionFit: A musical pitch symbol such as A flat, and a brief written message, share this word.

clue.text: Fortune left to provide part of church

parts.note: fortune means luck or chance

explanation.surface: Luck lets someone furnish a section of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the area around the altar, reserved for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Down like Jack?

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Jack fell down; a jack is also a chap, so a chap who has fallen, and down means dejected

explanation.surface: Feeling low, the way Jack did in the rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack of 'Jack and Jill' fell down the hill; take Jack as a chap and fell as fallen, while down also means dejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispirited, literally with the jaw hanging slack, describes someone whose mood has sunk.

clue.text: Cut-rate animals

indicators.note: cut tells us to clip a letter from the word for rate

parts.note: to rate is to assess or value

explanation.surface: Creatures sold off at a cheap price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut-rate' reads as one word meaning cheap; split it, and 'Cut' trims the last S from ASSESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkeys are beasts of burden, so they are a kind of animal.

clue.text: US city's Greek character 1884?

parts.note: chi is the twenty-second letter of the Greek alphabet
for a puzzle printed in 1984, the year 1884 was C (a hundred, in Roman numerals) years ago

explanation.surface: An American city's Greek character dated to 1884.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that '1884' is not a date in the city's history but a time a century before the puzzle appeared: C AGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a major city in Illinois, on Lake Michigan.

clue.text: Loyal subject of European city

definitions.meaning: a vassal owing feudal allegiance to a lord
a French-speaking city on the Meuse in eastern Belgium

explanation.definitionFit: A feudal vassal bound in allegiance, and a Belgian city spelt the same without its accent.

clue.text: Full-length sort of book that's not been read

definitions.meaning: not shortened or edited, as a film shown in full

definitions.text: sort of book that's not been read
definitions.meaning: old books had folded pages that had to be slit open before reading

explanation.definitionFit: Unabridged material, and a book whose folded page edges have never been slit open, both earn this word.

clue.text: Happen as result of a printer's error

indicators.note: a printer's error jumbles type, so these letters come out in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Something occurs because of a typesetting mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' signals the anagram: the letters of A PRINTERS rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To come about or occur; the sense grew from the idea of a fact leaking out.

clue.text: Greek islander arrested on return

indicators.note: on return tells us to read the word for arrested backwards

parts.note: nailed is slang for caught or arrested

explanation.surface: A Greek from one of the islands is taken into custody on coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Delos, the small Cycladic island sacred to Apollo.

clue.text: Having left vehicle, out of sight of house

parts.note: off means departed, as in 'they're off'
a stage is a stagecoach, a horse-drawn vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone who has got out of a car and is now hidden from the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The house is the theatre audience, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the house is the audience, and the wings are where actors stand unseen by it.

clue.text: Part of larynx: very quiet in water

indicators.note: in places the very quiet letters inside the term for water

parts.note: Adam's ale is an old jocular name for water
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet

explanation.surface: Part of the voice box is completely silent under water.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's ale, water, is the only drink the first man had.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulge at the front of the throat is formed by the thyroid cartilage of the voice box.

clue.text: Magnificent pair of lads contracted

parts.note: the first lad is Reg, short for Reginald
the second lad is Al, short for Albert or Alan

explanation.surface: A splendid couple of young men have signed a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' says each lad's name is shortened: Reginald to REG and Albert to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit for a king, so splendid and stately.

clue.text: Painter of the cross in his own country

parts.note: de is French for of
la is the French feminine word for the
croix is French for cross

explanation.surface: An artist who painted the cross while in his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in his own country' tells us to translate into French, the painter's language.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugène Delacroix was the leading French Romantic artist of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: What leader of circus in ring stands for

definitions.text: What leader of circus in ring stands for

parts.words: What leader of circus in ring stands for
parts.note: the leader of circus is C, and a C inside a ring is the symbol for a legal right over published work

explanation.surface: What the ringmaster at the big top represents.
explanation.walkthrough: Leader of circus sounds like the ringmaster, but it is the letter C; drawn in a ring it is the familiar © symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The © mark claims exclusive legal ownership of a work's reproduction rights.

clue.text: :Spouse that's cross? Happen it might be

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A wife who is angry? It could happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' turns HAPPEN IT into ANTHIPPE, after X for 'cross'. Socrates's wife was famous for a shrewish temper, so the cross spouse fits the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanthippe was the wife of the philosopher Socrates.

clue.text: Curriculum for backward girl. includes Greek

indicators.note: includes signals that the whole run takes the Greek letters within it

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the girl's name back to front

parts.note: Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A school course for a slow girl contains Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like a description of a slow pupil, but it is the reversal signal; 'includes' then makes the Greek abbreviation sit inside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A planned course of study is a syllabus or schedule of lessons.

clue.text: Before test, cricket side's being judged

indicators.note: before places the cricket side first, ahead of the word for test

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field; the 's is 'is'
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: Ahead of the Test match, the cricket team is under scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'test' suggests a cricket Test match but is a plain trial. In cricket the on side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone facing a court hearing is having their case decided by a judge or jury.

clue.text: Clearly not fair

explanation.definitionFit: Obviously or frankly, and homely rather than beautiful, are both senses of this word.

clue.text: A superior sort of accomplice .

parts.note: better means superior

explanation.surface: A higher class of partner in crime.
explanation.definitionFit: One who aids and encourages a wrongdoer is an accessory to the crime.

clue.text: Type of witness needed in suit

definitions.meaning: a witness whose evidence bears on the case
cloth needed to make a suit of clothes

explanation.definitionFit: Evidence that is relevant to a legal case, and the fabric from which clothes are made, share this word.

clue.text: Old man in tree climbs up another

indicators.note: in a down clue climbs up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
in places the father inside the tree

parts.note: elm is a tree
pa is an informal word for father, an old man

explanation.surface: An elderly chap in a tree clambers up a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition: another tree, after the ELM. Reading ELPAM upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple is a second kind of tree, following the elm already mentioned.

clue.text: Come back with old French coin among sovereigns

indicators.note: among puts the coin between the two royal letters

parts.note: R stands for rex, king, so two sovereigns are RR
the ecu was an old French coin

explanation.surface: Return with an ancient French coin found among gold sovereigns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereigns' suggests British gold coins, but it means monarchs: R for Rex, twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen again or reappear is to return.

clue.text: Audibly break part of arm

indicators.note: audibly means the word for break is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a breach is a break or gap

explanation.surface: A loud fracture in part of someone's arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like a limb but is a firearm: the breech is the back of a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear section of a gun barrel, where the cartridge is loaded, belongs to a firearm.

clue.text: Head announced for — political alliance

indicators.note: announced means the word for head is spoken out

parts.note: block is slang for the head, as in 'knock your block off'

explanation.surface: A leader is declared for a coalition of parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouping of nations or parties acting together for a common purpose.

clue.text: Sort of boy that isn't really most important

definitions.text: Sort of boy that isn't really
definitions.meaning: in British pantomime the young male hero is traditionally played by a woman

explanation.walkthrough: In British pantomime, a Christmas stage show, the leading 'boy' role is played by an actress.
explanation.definitionFit: The panto hero played by an actress, and chief or leading, share this word.

clue.text: Rose is dressed

definitions.meaning: stood up, got out of bed
decked out in clothes or costume

explanation.definitionFit: Getting out of bed, and being decked out in a costume, are both expressed by this phrase.

clue.text: Elaborate changes, in general

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Detailed alterations, broadly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' looks like a noun but is the verb, rearranging GENERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate on a point is to expand it with more detail.

clue.text: Set in lake, on bed

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the lake after the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Positioned in a lake, resting on a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a verb (placed) but is the noun for a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusive clique of people with shared interests forms a close circle.
